findings.evidence: Line 366 `(hRc : Continuous (R.merge a)) (hJc : Continuous fun v : V => J (v ::ₘ t))`; proof uses only `(hJc.comp hRc).tendsto 0` (line 372). Roadmap JetsAndEventShapes/README.md:111-116: "Safety is a limit condition, not continuity … a recombination algorithm's jet multiplicity is not [continuous] … The trap avoided is assuming continuity and so proving nothing."
findings.fix: Weaken `hRc`/`hJc` to `ContinuousAt (R.merge a) 0` and `ContinuousAt (fun v => J (v ::ₘ t)) a` (the composition argument goes through unchanged, and `continuous_eScheme_merge` still supplies the first), and state the observable-side hypothesis explicitly in both docstrings, saying that it is a regularity assumption on `J` at `a` which a discontinuous observable such as jet multiplicity meets only away from ties.
findings.issue: `IsUnital.tendsto_cons` requires `hJc : Continuous fun v : V => J (v ::ₘ t)` — continuity of the clustering observable in the merged momentum slot — but neither its own docstring (lines 358-363, which lists only `hR`, `hRc` and `hJ`) nor the module docstring (lines 32-33, "a unital scheme with a continuous merge map absorbs a vanishingly soft momentum") mentions it. That is the strongest hypothesis of the lemma and it excludes the motivating observable: jet multiplicity is not continuous in the momenta, and roadmap convention 5 names assuming continuity as "the trap avoided" (README lines 111-116). Both `Continuous` hypotheses are also stronger than the proof needs — only `ContinuousAt (R.merge a) 0` and `ContinuousAt (fun v => J (v ::ₘ t)) a` are used.

findings.evidence: Line 121 `∀ p : V, ∀ z ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1, …`; line 171 `∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ p : V, R.merge p (t • p) = (1 + t) • p`; docstring lines 166-169 "a scheme that rescales a merged pair to make it massless with respect to a frame meets it at the massless momenta". Roadmap README:356-357 describes the `p`/`E₀` schemes as rescaling the sum to be massless, which for a massive parallel pair changes `(1 + t) • p`.
findings.fix: Relativise the criterion to a set closed under nonnegative scalars — e.g. `IsCollinearExactOn (C : Set V)` and `∀ p ∈ C, ∀ t ≥ 0, merge p (t • p) = (1 + t) • p` (both directions of the current proof localise to such a cone unchanged) — or drop the applicability sentences and say only that a restricted variant will be needed.
findings.issue: `IsCollinearExact` (line 121) and the right-hand side of `IsHomogeneous.isCollinearExact_iff` (line 171) quantify over all `p : V`, yet the docstrings (lines 165-169, 41-44, 202-204) assert this is the criterion the frame-dependent schemes that rescale a merged pair to masslessness "meet at the massless momenta". Those schemes satisfy neither side as stated: for a massive `p`, the sum `(1 + t) • p` of the parallel pair is massive and the scheme rescales it, so `merge p (t • p) ≠ (1 + t) • p`. The lemma as formulated therefore cannot be applied to them even on the massless cone, so the claim about what remains of §0.6 once `Frame` lands is not supported by what is proved here.

summary: All new statements are mathematically faithful and non-vacuous; the E-scheme rigidity and the homogeneous exactness criterion both check out, and the correction to the milestone is sound. Two hypothesis/docstring mismatches need fixing: `IsUnital.tendsto_cons` silently assumes continuity of the observable itself (the trap convention 5 names), and the exactness criterion is quantified over all of `V`, so it cannot be met by the massless-restoring schemes the docstrings say it serves.
